judged_text: Host format regex anchored with \A/\Z instead of \z, allowing a host value ending in newline followed by malicious content to bypass validation

record.issue_text: Host format regex anchored with \A/\Z instead of \z, allowing a host value ending in newline followed by malicious content to bypass validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbeddableHost` with `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A...\Z/i`. In Ruby, `\Z` can match before a final trailing newline, so a value like `"example.com\n"` could pass validation. However, the proposed finding claims it allows `"example.com\n<malicious content>"` (newline followed by extra content) to bypass validation, which is not true: `\Z` will not match if there is any content after that newline (it only ignores a newline at the very end). So the specific bypass described is a misread. At most, there’s a minor issue allowing a trailing newline character, not “newline + malicious content”.
